sections.title: Form and flowers
sections.text: Tanacetum vulgare is an aromatic, upright perennial, usually about 0.6–1 m tall and 0.1–0.5 m wide in cultivation. Its deeply divided leaves may reach 10 cm; clusters of button-like yellow flower heads, about 5–9 mm across, appear in summer and autumn. The plate agrees with this form.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The plant contains thujone and is poisonous if eaten; ingestion can cause serious neurological and liver effects. It may also irritate skin. Do not use its leaves or flower heads as food or tea.

sections.title: Range and uses
sections.text: Native to Europe, tansy grows on grassland, roadsides and disturbed ground. Its strong-smelling foliage has been used as an insect repellent, but that use does not make it safe to ingest.
